question_text: How many Supreme Court justices are usually needed to decide a case?

why_it_matters.text: Five out of nine is a simple majority — the smallest number of justices who can make a ruling stick. That's why so many of the biggest Supreme Court decisions are 5-4 splits. A single vote can shape the law for generations. The Court's decisions aren't always unanimous, but the majority rules.

fun_fact.text: Five of the nine justices need to agree to make a ruling stick. But what if they tie 4-4? That happens when a seat is vacant or a justice steps aside. In that case, the lower court's decision is upheld — but no nationwide precedent is set. After Justice Scalia's death in 2016, several major cases ended in 4-4 ties.
